reads.what_it_sells: Repairboard offers a shared repair-status board that I would update with each job’s current stage and could let customers inspect through a read-only link.
reads.relevance_feedback: The profile explicitly says I am considering how customers can inspect repair stages, and the email offers exactly that through a read-only status link. The email additionally presupposes that a shared board could fit my shop, but my current workflow, customer-information needs, and willingness to maintain another system are unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I am considering ways for customers to inspect repair stages.
Email-only: My shop could use a shared board to display every repair’s current stage.
Email-only: A read-only status link may provide the right amount of information for my customers.
Unknown: How repair stages are currently tracked or communicated in my shop.
reads.problem_now: Customer visibility into repair stages is an explicitly relevant consideration, but the profile establishes no urgency, deadline, or current communication failure. The sample is still a proportionate next step because it can be inspected without committing to adoption.
reads.biggest_doubt: I do not know whether viewing the sample requires signup or how much work the board would add to keeping repair stages current, so I might postpone opening another link before my meeting.
reads.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me the sample opens without signup and can be assessed in under a minute.
fixes: Rewrite "The sample shows the board directly" as "Open the sample directly—no signup—to see both the shop board and the customer’s read-only view."

Rewrite "Take a look at how the stages appear and whether the customer-facing view provides the right level of information for your shop." as "Compare the shop board with the read-only customer view and decide whether it shows the right repair details."
